en: Well... Typically, driving a car is more convenient. But I'll take a train if it's better to do so.
I see. I always see the streets in Tokyo being gridlocked with traffic, but I can see how trains are less convenient in Nagoya.
Yes, here in Nagoya our roadways are nice and wide, so traffic flows more easily. You can reach some impressive speeds as well!
That's cool! You can't get the thrill of flying down the road in a train.
Oh my, you like to drive as well, Shinada-san? Perhaps you could take me out on a drive sometime!
Hey, you bet! Just as soon as I can actually get one...
That's no good. Driving fast like that could put other drivers at risk.
But driving slowly takes so much time. What else are people supposed to do?
You people need to relax some more. You guys are all rich, what's there to be rushing about?
Trains are more convenient. You can do so many other things with your time en route. Like take a nap.
How unseemly, sleeping in front of other people! I prefer the privacy offered by being inside my own vehicle.
I guess if you put it like that...
It's not normal at all. One family might own a single car, if that. It's super rare for a family to have one car per person.
But if a family only has one car, what do the others do if someone has already taken it out? Do they call for a town car?
Sure, if you're rich. They probably only take the train if they've been drinking and can't drive.
Oh, but if I have my car and I've been drinking, I can simply have my chauffeur drive.
Chauffeur!? What color is the sky in your world, anyhow?
Then you take the train. Seriously, you can take the train basically anywhere.
Oh, now I get it! I always found it curious why people would take the train instead of using their own car.
Hey, that's privilege for you.
I'm guessing it's a foreign model? Man, it must be nice to be rich.
Oh, I wish you could have one too, Shinada-san. I think a sports car would suit you quite well!
Sweet! I'll buy one! I just have to save up the cash. How much do you think it'll cost?
A new car would be around 15 million yen, maybe? Limited edition models would run around 30 million, but I wouldn't recommend those.
Whoa, seriously!? That's insane!
Oh my, is it? Well, if you can't afford a new car, perhaps you can negotiate for a secondhand one.
Ha, maybe if they could bring down the price by one, preferably two decimal places.
No frickin' way. I wouldn't even make it past the credit check. And even if I did, the yearly maintenance cost would break my nonexistent piggy bank.
That really can't be avoided, though. It's like your gas and water bill⑬ a necessary living expense.
No, this would definitely be a luxury. Unless I lived in the sticks and could somehow find a house with a garage, I could never afford to have one.
Couldn't you park it in front of your house even without a garage? I see many households around here do that.
I'm surprised people don't get ticketed for doing that. Nagoya really is another world.
I've noticed there's a lot of coffee shops around here.
Now that you mention it, I suppose there are.
More than convenience stores, even. I bet there isn't a city in all of Japan that has as many coffee shops as this place does.
Really? But I heard that there was a big café boom all over the country.
Yeah, but those are all foreign chain shops. They're more like fast-food places, so nothing like the mom-and-pop ones.
Yes, the atmosphere would be quite different. I had no idea.
Do you not go much?
No, we do. When I have tea with friends, for instance, we often go to a coffee shop or teahouse instead of someone's home.
Huh, wonder why everyone around here loves coffee shops so much?
It's quite relaxing. We wind up having long conversations, and can even spend the better part of the day there.
Do you go to them often as well, Shinada-san?
Of course! Practically every day. I like being able to go into a coffee shop and order up "the usual," hehe.
A cup of coffee with toast and a salad, throw in an egg on the side. That's the stuff!
Here, it's typical for shops to provide a complimentary accompaniment as well.
When I went to Tokyo, I was rather surprised when I wasn't served anything else with the coffee I had ordered.
That's typical. There are breakfast combos you can get, but they're not as cheap as in Nagoya.
I feel 500 yen for a single cup of coffee is far too expensive.
Heh, even by your standards?
Nagoya's the best. Now that I've lived here, I don't think I could stand living anywhere else.
I'm so delighted you like it!
Speaking of our coffee shops, they really do feel more like restaurants, don't they?
It's actually not uncommon for families to go to coffee shops for breakfast on weekends and holidays, to give mothers a break from cooking.
Sounds like a good time. I always had baseball practice in the morning, so I never could have a family breakfast like that.
Yeah. So the owner of the coffee shop sort of became like family to me.
Oh my! In that case, would you be so kind as to introduce me to this coffee shop of yours? I'd love to go if you're so fond of it, Shinada-san.
You got it! I'm sure you'll love it!
How does that turn out? I like to skip breakfast on my days off, so I can stay in bed and sleep more.
Oh dear. Don't you think you should value time spent with your family more? It's rare for a family to be able to go out and eat together.
That doesn't mean it's gotta be in the morning. Why not go out for dinner instead?
But it's troublesome to wake up early to cook breakfast. You really should appreciate the effort mothers of the world go through, Shinada-san.
I hear what you're saying, but there's just no way I can wake up that early.
Can I come next time, too?
Oh my, are you offering to take me out?
Yeah! I have a customer loyalty card at this coffee shop, so if I buy ten cups, I get the eleventh one free!
I must say, I would prefer you not to be so stingy about our date!
Oh, uh... I was joking! Honest! Just the humor of broke people, heh.
You Nagoya gals sure are amazing. Compared to girls in Osaka, you're way more... How should I put it? More glamorous? Well, at least more flashy!
I hear that a lot, actually. Do you really think so too, Shinada-san?
Absolutely! I've been all over Japan, and no other city has such glittery girls like you packing the streets.
Oh, really? I do strive to be fashionable, but it's still quite humbling to be given a compliment like that.
No need to be shy! I think it's great!
On second thought, not so much. Like that's what I imagined, but reality seems to be coming up a little short.
I see. In what way does is not live up to your expectations? Are Tokyo girls more showy? I'm rather curious.
Yep, Tokyo has you beat. You ladies are no match for the ones in Shibuya or Roppongi.
Well, now! I had no idea.
I'll have to ask my mother to buy me better clothing at once. I will not be outdone.
It's the same everywhere, really. Trends seem to hit the whole country at once nowadays.
How true. It isn't as if Nagoya is the lone trendsetter.
I would've thought it'd be a bit slower to reach here, actually.
But the girls here do all wear nice clothing. And it's all designer stuff at that.
I suppose so, but is that not the case in any affluent region?
That's true. I guess the rich just outnumber the flashy, huh?
Indeed. I'm sure certain areas where the wealthy gather in Tokyo feel just like Nagoya.
Maybe so. Heck, maybe it's just us regular folk that notice anything at all. The rich probably think Nagoya's as normal as it gets.
Hmph! I'm afraid I'll have to stop you there. I don't appreciate you putting down my city like that.
Hey, does it really matter what I think anyways? You've got so much pride!
Not at all. You should check out Tokyo. Then you'll see what makes Nagoya so special.
Oh, that could be fun! But it would be so boring to go by myself. Perhaps I'll go with my friends!
That'll be one group of tourists that really stands out.
Oh no. They might be loaded, but that doesn't mean they obsess over designer stuff. They just wear normal clothes, like me and you. Er, well, like me.
Oh my, really? I don't like feeling as if people in Nagoya spend money carelessly.
In any case, if it were only about being rich, the men would be just as showy, right? But it's only the girls. Weird...
Perhaps women need to attract more attention to themselves?
Without a doubt. Compared to them, the men might as well be country bumpkins.
I quite agree! I wonder, why don't men here have refined sensibilities?
You got me there. Hahaha.
It's not that. I think the girls here are all pretty humble, actually.
Then why did you say that girls in Nagoya are so brand-obsessed?
You speak in such vague terms about everything, Shinada-san! I don't get your point!
Well, if I spoke my mind, you'd probably get offended.
It's because of the makeup. Like, guys don't wear makeup, right? That's why it's only the girls who stand out.
But don't women all over the country wear makeup?
Yeah, but here the girls lay it on real thick. Don't people say that a lot, that it's because the girls here are actually ugly?
Well, I never! Even if that's how you feel, I'd rather you not go and say it out loud!
Ack, sorry! Uh, I was kidding, I swear!
Did you know that tequila's popular with foreign celebrities? It started in Hollywood, so now everyone in the States is crazy about it.
My word, isn't tequila a spirit that's rather high in alcohol? I imagine a woman like myself would find it quite harsh.
Nah, it's only between 35 and 55 percent alcohol, so it's much weaker than vodka. Vodka can go as high as 90 percent.
And if it's premium, one hundred percent agave tequila, the alcohol is processed faster, so even ladies can drink it without getting sick.
Oh, really? I'm rather curious what it tastes like. The next time I go to a bar I may have to try some!
Heh, a tequila-drinkin' gal would be right up my alley!
Since my mother is from France, I'm more accustomed to drinking wine and champagne.
Though I've heard that more recently, young people in France don't drink wine very much.
It's probably for the best. Drinking too much isn't good for you, and it isn't exactly a cheap habit.
I hear young people in Japan don't drink beer much anymore, either. But I always like a drink and good conversation.
Oh, that's right. I had my picture taken while I was drunk the other day. I saw the photo later and my face looked hideous.
Hehe, were you beet red?
My mouth was open in this tremendous laugh, as if something were particularly amusing. I had lost any and all sense of shame!
Haha! I'd like to see you like that, Shion-chan!
Oh, but I'd rather not drink again for a while.
Oh, that's right. Sorry.
I go out for drinks at bars from time to time, and men often try to hit on me.
That's because you're so pretty. Even if they're married, I bet they can't help but flirt.
Quite so! I do prefer that to men who would ignore a catch like myself!
Heh, not lacking in confidence, are you?
Shinada-san, you told me about this already.
Oh no, did I?
I'd rather talk about something else.
Do you ever go to the ballpark to watch baseball games, Shion-chan?
Only once, I'm afraid.
I was too far away to see much, and it was quite too rowdy for me. I left partway through.
Why not try watching from a VIP skybox?
Oh, are there special rooms like that?
Yep! VIP rooms give you a great view of the field. You can even sit on a sofa and watch the game in the peace and quiet.
And even better, there are monitors all over so you can see close-ups on the big plays. Oh, and you can order food and drinks, right from the box! It's a great way to enjoy a game.
That sounds lovely! Knowing that there are rooms like that, I may have to try going to see another game sometime.
You bet! I'd love to try one of them out someday, too.
Speaking of which, when I went to the race track the other day, my ears hurt quite a bit from the noise.
Oh yeah, I hear you need earplugs to watch F1.
After that, the crowd at a ball game is downright silent! Perhaps I overreacted.
Heh, maybe next time you should join in the cheering.
Baseball is rather popular in America, isn't it? I know they have basketball and football too, but I feel baseball is their national sport.
